newsitem.title: UK: UK NATGAS RANGEBOUND AS BUYERS, SELLERS HOLD FIRM.
newsitem.headline: UK NATGAS RANGEBOUND AS BUYERS, SELLERS HOLD FIRM.

text.p: The U.K. natural gas spot market held in a tight range on Wednesday with neither buyers nor sellers willing to compromise an inch.
Prices went to four decimal places as traders fought over thousandths of a pennies.
"It's very tight indeed, the bid/ask ranges are so tight on some months it's ridiculous," said one trader. "No-one is prepared to give."
But the close ranges produced a flurry of deals with most quarters across the forward curve traded.
Values for prompt gas were unchanged from Tuesday with within day gas, entry paid at Theddlethorpe, traded at 9.55 pence a therm (p/th) and day ahead done at 9.55 and 9.50 p/th.
September was heavily traded, at a low of 9.45 p/th at the NBP and a high of 9.60 p/th at Bacton.
First quarter 1998 was fiercely fought over, with deals done at Tuesday's level of 17.20 p/th, and also at 17.2125 p/th and 17.1875 p/th.
The second quarter traded flat on Tuesday's levels while the third quarter traded several times in the 10.45 p/th range.
"You can practically hear this market creaking...Something's going to give soon," said one trader.
The futures market saw another busy day's trade with over 400 lots done. But news of a "busted", or cancelled deal in the morning session overshadowed proceedings.
A trade for was 100 lots, or 100,000 therms a day, was done on September at 0.95 pence a therm (p/th) after a seller erroneously inputted the offer at that price instead of at 9.50 p/th.
The IPE cancelled the deal saying it was "a manifest error".
If the trade had not been busted the mistake would have cost the seller 256,500 stg.
The spokeswoman said that the Exchange would cancel trades if a clear mistake is made in order "to ensure an orderly market".
But some market players said that busted trades harmed the Exchange's credibility.
